summary: The current recce/services/modbus.py implements a minimal reachability + banner probe (Functions 0x03 and 0x2B/0x0E Basic). It skips the majority of Modbus/TCP's attacker-relevant surface: unit-ID enumeration through TCP-to-RTU gateways, diagnostics subfunctions (including Force Listen-Only DoS), Read Exception Status, Report Slave ID, safer register/coil reads that fingerprint process state, vendor-specific function codes (Schneider UMAS 0x5A, Siemens, Codesys), the Modbus Security (TLS/802) side-channel, and any CVE-level firmware/product matching. It also does not feed vendor/model/serial data into cross-service pools (creds, asset inventory, downstream-device lists behind gateways).
existing_capabilities: TCP connect to 502/8502 with is_modbus port/service/product match
Function 0x03 Read Holding Registers (addr=0, count=1) with unit-ID rotation across (1,0,255)
Function 0x2B/0x0E Read Device Identification, Basic conformity level 0x01, objects VendorName(0)/ProductCode(1)/MajorMinorRevision(2)
HIGH finding on reachable, INFO finding on device ID, static runbook (modpoll/mbtget)
Read-only design: never writes to the device

missing_capabilities.name: Unit-ID / slave-ID sweep across gateway
missing_capabilities.description: Modbus/TCP-to-RTU gateways are extremely common. Sweeping unit IDs 0-247 (MODBUS Application Protocol v1.1b3 §4.1) discovers downstream serial PLCs hiding behind the TCP endpoint. Currently only 1/0/255 are tried and only to satisfy the first success — so the whole downstream fleet is invisible. Each responding unit is a distinct target and should feed the cross-service inventory.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MODBUS Application Protocol v1.1b3 §4.1 (Unit Identifier) and MODBUS Messaging on TCP/IP v1.0b §3.1.3

missing_capabilities.name: Function 0x11 Report Server/Slave ID
missing_capabilities.description: Returns vendor-specific controller data + run-indicator byte. On Schneider/Modicon, AB, and older devices this yields firmware banner and running state that Function 0x2B does not. Not implemented.

missing_capabilities.name: Function 0x2B/0x0E Regular (0x02) and Extended (0x03) conformity reads
missing_capabilities.description: Only Basic (0x01, objects 0-2) is read. Regular pulls VendorUrl(3), ProductName(4), ModelName(5), UserApplicationName(6); Extended pulls vendor-defined objects 0x80+ (serials, MAC, project name, download timestamps). This is the main asset-fingerprint layer.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MODBUS App Protocol v1.1b3 §6.21 (MEI Type 0x0E, ReadDevID codes 0x01/0x02/0x03/0x04)

missing_capabilities.name: Function 0x07 Read Exception Status
missing_capabilities.description: Serial-legacy but supported by many bridged/embedded stacks. Returns 8 status bits — device-specific but often reveals alarm/run states. Zero cost, high signal for legacy device fingerprinting.

missing_capabilities.name: Function 0x08 Diagnostics subfunctions (0x00, 0x0B-0x12)
missing_capabilities.description: Return Query Data (0x00) proves the endpoint is really a Modbus stack; Return Bus/Slave counters (0x0B-0x12) leak connection statistics, error counts and identify the device family. Currently unprobed.

missing_capabilities.name: Function 0x08 sub 0x04 Force Listen-Only Mode — DoS primitive
missing_capabilities.description: One MBAP frame silences the target — device stops responding on Modbus until a Restart Comms (sub 0x01) or power cycle. Iconic OT DoS attack (used in CrashOverride/Industroyer). Should be an opt-in EXPLOIT capability so operators can prove segmentation risk; currently absent. Also implicitly: sub 0x01 (Restart Communications Option) — can clear counters or restart comms.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MODBUS App Protocol v1.1b3 §6.8 subfunction 0x04 (Force Listen Only Mode); ICS-CERT ICSA-16-336-04

missing_capabilities.name: Function 0x01/0x02/0x04 (Coils, Discrete Inputs, Input Registers)
missing_capabilities.description: Only Holding Registers (0x03) is read. Coils and Discrete Inputs reveal process I/O state (valves open/closed, contactors); Input Registers reveal live sensor telemetry. Reading these is fingerprint-quality proof of a running process and lets us distinguish an idle test rig from a live PLC.

missing_capabilities.name: Write-capability probe (0x05/0x06/0x0F/0x10) via safe echo-write
missing_capabilities.description: A non-destructive write test — read a coil/register, write the SAME value back, observe ack vs exception 0x01/0x02/0x04 — proves whether the device accepts writes from this network position. That elevates modbus_reachable from HIGH to CRITICAL (attacker can move a valve, not just watch). Currently the finding assumes writability without evidence.

missing_capabilities.name: Schneider UMAS (Function 0x5A) probe — CVE-2018-7846, CVE-2020-7475, CVE-2021-22779
missing_capabilities.description: Schneider M221/M340/M580 tunnel their programming protocol (UMAS) over Modbus function 0x5A. Multiple pre-auth abuses: session hijacking (CVE-2021-22779), project upload/download without auth (CVE-2020-7475), reserved-command RCE (CVE-2018-7846). A one-byte probe (function 0x5A, subfunction 0x02 Read ID) confirms UMAS is exposed. Nothing in the module knows about vendor function codes.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Schneider UMAS Reference (function code 90); NVD CVE-2018-7846, CVE-2020-7475, CVE-2021-22779, CVE-2022-45789

missing_capabilities.name: Siemens SIMATIC / Codesys runtime on 502 detection
missing_capabilities.description: Codesys V2/V3 runtimes often expose Modbus/TCP alongside their own protocol on 1200/2455; a device answering Modbus with a Codesys product banner is affected by a large CVE cluster (CVE-2022-31806, CVE-2022-32136, CVE-2023-3663) — no fingerprint layer to catch this. Same for SIMATIC S7-1200 Modbus DoS CVE-2019-10920.

missing_capabilities.name: Modbus Security (TLS) probe on port 802
missing_capabilities.description: The 'Modbus Security' spec (Modbus.org, 2018) defines TLS-wrapped MBAP on TCP/802 with X.509 client auth carrying a role OID. Recce doesn't scan 802 or attempt a TLS ClientHello there. A device that supports 802 but ALSO leaves 502 open is a much sharper finding than 502-only, and a device only on 802 gets missed entirely.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MODBUS/TCP Security v21 (2018) §5 (TCP/802, TLS 1.2+ w/ role-based X.509 extension)

missing_capabilities.name: Malformed-PDU / oversize-length fuzzing markers (Aegis-style)
missing_capabilities.description: Well-known family of MBAP crashes: length field > 260 (spec max §4.1), unit-ID 248-255 reserved usage (§4.1), function 0x2B with invalid MEI 0x0D — many embedded stacks (Modicon <=v2.4, ProSoft, Wago, older Advantech) crash. Should be an opt-in ACTIVE check gated behind explicit exploit-mode, since it can actually hang the PLC.

missing_capabilities.name: Function code enumeration / exception-code mapping
missing_capabilities.description: Sending each standard fn 0x01-0x18 and 0x2B, and cataloguing which return normal / exception 0x01 (Illegal Function) / 0x04 (Slave Device Failure), fingerprints the stack (Modicon vs open-source libmodbus vs freemodbus vs Codesys) very precisely. Zero writes, one round-trip per function. Not implemented.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MODBUS App Protocol v1.1b3 §7 Exception responses (codes 01-0B)

missing_capabilities.name: Cross-service wire: downstream unit list
missing_capabilities.description: When the endpoint is a gateway, each responding unit-ID represents a distinct downstream device that should appear as its own target row (with unit-ID) and be included in target inventory, downstream_devices pool, and vendor-specific finding routing. Right now those devices are invisible to the rest of recce.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MODBUS Messaging on TCP/IP v1.0b §3.1.3 (routing via Unit ID)

missing_capabilities.name: Cross-service wire: vendor/model to CVE + default-cred pools
missing_capabilities.description: Device-ID vendor/product/revision is captured then only echoed in a finding string — never normalized (SchneiderElectric/M340/v3.10 -> canonical vendor+model+version tuple) and never fed to shared vendor_products / known_default_creds pools. That's how Schneider 'admin/blank', Siemens 'Administrator/(blank)', Allen-Bradley Micro8xx creds get missed by later HTTP/FTP/Telnet probes on the same host.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: MODBUS App Protocol v1.1b3 §6.21 objects 0-2; ICS-CERT default-cred advisories per vendor

missing_capabilities.name: Cross-service wire: extended device-ID serial/MAC to hostnames/asset inventory
missing_capabilities.description: Extended objects (0x80+) commonly carry MAC, serial number, project name and station name — asset-identity data that should populate known_hostnames and asset inventory pools for reporting and cross-host correlation. Not read, not exported.

missing_capabilities.name: Elevated severity path when write is proven
missing_capabilities.description: modbus_reachable is fixed at HIGH regardless of whether writes are accepted. If a safe echo-write probe succeeds (see above), the finding should re-emit at CRITICAL with a CWE-1287/CWE-284 tag and a distinct kind ('modbus_writable') so ranking, exploit-session generation, and dashboards route it correctly.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Derived from §6.5/6.6/6.11/6.12 write functions + §7 exception responses

priority_gaps: Function 0x08 sub 0x04 Force Listen-Only Mode DoS probe (opt-in exploit)
Unit-ID 0-247 sweep to discover downstream RTU slaves behind TCP-to-RTU gateways
Safe echo-write probe using 0x05/0x06 to prove writability and elevate finding to CRITICAL
Schneider UMAS function 0x5A detection for CVE-2018-7846 / CVE-2020-7475 / CVE-2021-22779
Function 0x2B/0x0E Regular + Extended conformity reads (ModelName, UserAppName, serial/MAC via 0x80+)
Modbus Security TLS probe on TCP/802
Function 0x11 Report Server ID + 0x07 Read Exception Status for legacy device fingerprint
Cross-service export: normalized vendor/product/revision + downstream unit-IDs into shared pools (asset inventory, default-cred routing, CVE match)
Function 0x01/0x02/0x04 reads to prove live process state (elevates from 'device on network' to 'live process on network')
Function-code enumeration + exception-code fingerprint for stack identification (Codesys, libmodbus, Modicon)
cross_service_wire_gaps: Downstream unit-IDs discovered behind a gateway are not emitted as separate targets or into a shared downstream_devices pool
Vendor/product/revision from 0x2B is only inlined into the finding text — never normalized nor pushed to a vendor_products/known_default_creds pool for other services on the same host
Extended device-ID objects (serial, MAC, project name, station name) are not fetched and therefore never fed to known_hostnames / asset-inventory pools
No feedback to a relay_targets or cred pool from vendor-string ('Schneider' -> admin/blank on HTTP, 'Siemens' -> Administrator/blank, 'Rockwell' -> guest, etc.)
modbus_reachable finding severity does not chain to a modbus_writable exploit primitive when writes succeed — no exploit-session artefact emitted for the exploit-session-wiring pipeline
notes: Scope reminder: recce is airgap-constrained, so all recommended probes must remain stdlib socket+struct with no external CVE lookup at runtime — CVE matching should be a shipped local vendor/version table keyed by the normalized fingerprint. All ACTIVE items (Force Listen-Only, write echo, malformed-PDU fuzz, UMAS reserved commands) must sit behind explicit exploit-mode gates because they can genuinely disrupt a physical process; the punch list flags them but they should not run in the default passive scan path.
